15-1252.what: You write the code that makes apps, websites and games work.
15-1252.day: Sit down at a computer, break a big problem into small pieces, write code for each one, then test it to see what breaks.
15-1252.school: Computer science, maths, and lots of practice building things

29-1141.what: You look after sick and injured people in hospitals, clinics and schools.
29-1141.day: Check on your patients, give them medicine, help doctors, write down what you did, and hand over to the next nurse.

11-3021.what: You run a company's computer systems and the team that looks after them.
11-3021.day: Meet with your team, plan what projects to start, explain technical stuff to people who are not technical, and deal with problems when a system goes down.

15-1232.what: You help people fix their computer problems, usually over the phone or by visiting their desk.
15-1232.day: Answer calls, work out what is wrong, walk people through the fix step by step, and write down what you did.
15-1232.school: Computer science, and practice explaining things clearly

29-2061.what: You care for patients in hospitals, nursing homes and doctor's offices under a nurse's direction.
29-2061.day: Help people wash, dress and eat, check on them through the night, and keep the nurse updated about how they are doing.

15-1211.what: You work out what a company needs its computers to do, and help build it.
15-1211.day: Talk to the people who will use the system, write down what they need, test the software, and fix the parts that do not work.

29-2052.what: You do most of the behind-the-scenes work in a pharmacy, like filling prescriptions.
29-2052.day: Take prescriptions, count and label medicine, answer phone calls, and help customers find what they need.

15-1299.what: You do computing jobs that do not have their own special name, like database work or tech support.
15-1299.day: It depends on the job, but usually it means using computers to solve a problem for a team.

11-9121.what: You lead a team of scientists and make sure their research gets done properly.
11-9121.day: Plan research projects, write proposals for funding, check on experiments, and present results.
11-9121.school: Science, then a degree in research or management

29-1171.what: You are a nurse who can diagnose and treat patients, usually in a doctor's office.
29-1171.day: See patients, examine them, diagnose common problems, write prescriptions and treatment plans, and follow up later.
29-1171.school: Biology, chemistry, and a nursing degree

29-1123.what: You help people recover movement and strength after an injury or surgery.
29-1123.day: Work with patients, watch how they move, design exercises for them, and cheer them on as they get stronger.

29-1229.what: You are a doctor who treats patients in a hospital or clinic.
29-1229.day: See patients, examine them, order tests, treat illness or injury, and write notes for the next doctor.
29-1229.school: Biology, chemistry, physics, then medical school

29-1051.what: You mix and dispense the medicine that doctors prescribe, and advise people how to use it safely.
29-1051.day: Check prescriptions, talk to doctors, counsel patients, and keep the shelves stocked.

15-1244.what: You keep an organisation's computers and networks running and secure.
15-1244.day: Set up and fix servers, watch for security problems, add new users, and make sure everything keeps working.

49-9041.what: You repair and maintain the big machines used in factories.
49-9041.day: Diagnose a broken machine, take it apart, replace worn parts, and get it running again.
49-9041.school: Physics, maths and hands-on technical work

29-1292.what: You clean people's teeth and prevent gum disease.
29-1292.day: Examine teeth, take x-rays, clean teeth, and teach people how to brush properly.

29-1129.what: You help people recover or cope using therapy of different kinds.
29-1129.day: Meet with patients, work out what would help them most, and run therapy sessions.

29-2010.what: You test blood and other samples to help doctors diagnose illness.
29-2010.day: Run lab tests on samples, check the results carefully, and report anything unusual to the doctor.

17-2051.what: You design roads, bridges, water systems and buildings so they are safe.
17-2051.day: Draw plans, work out loads and costs, check building sites, and make sure designs follow the rules.

17-2112.what: You make factories and businesses work better and waste less.
17-2112.day: Watch how work is actually done, time each step, and redesign it so it is faster, safer or cheaper.

29-1127.what: You help people who have trouble speaking, hearing or understanding language.
29-1127.day: Test how well a child or adult can hear and speak, then design exercises to help them improve.

15-1253.what: You test software to find the bugs before users do.
15-1253.day: Try to break the software in every way you can, write down exactly what went wrong, and check the fixes.
15-1253.school: Computer science and attention to detail

15-2051.what: You find useful patterns in huge amounts of data and help people make decisions with them.
15-2051.day: Clean data, write code to analyse it, build models, and explain the findings to people who are not scientists.

29-2034.what: You take x-ray pictures of people's bodies so doctors can see what is wrong.
29-2034.day: Position the patient, take the images, check the quality, and describe what you see for the doctor.

51-2028.what: You build electrical and electronic parts that go into phones, cars and machines.
51-2028.day: Set up and run assembly lines, check quality, fix faulty parts, and keep records of what was made.

29-1122.what: You help people get back to doing everyday tasks after an injury or illness.
29-1122.day: Plan what a patient needs to do again, practise it with them, and adapt the plan when it is hard.

19-1042.what: You study disease to work out what causes it and how to treat or stop it.
19-1042.day: Run experiments, look at results, write up what you found, and plan the next study.

29-2042.what: You are the first person to help people in an emergency before a doctor arrives.
29-2042.day: Respond to calls, treat injuries and illnesses on the scene, and drive the ambulance if needed.
29-2042.school: Biology, maths and first aid training

29-2099.what: You do health jobs that do not have a specific name, like running a clinic or medical equipment.
29-2099.day: Varies a lot, but usually means using health knowledge and technology to support doctors and patients.

15-1241.what: You design the networks that connect an organisation's computers together.
15-1241.day: Plan how data should move, set up the network equipment, and make it fast and safe.

19-2031.what: You study what things are made of and how they react with each other.
19-2031.day: Mix and test chemicals in a lab, record what happens, and check results against what other scientists found.

15-1212.what: You protect computers and data from people who try to break into them.
15-1212.day: Look for weaknesses, test systems, watch alerts for suspicious activity, and help staff stay safe.

29-1071.what: You are a medical professional who examines patients, diagnoses illness and treats them.
29-1071.day: See patients, examine them, order tests, prescribe treatment, and follow up on how they are doing.

11-9041.what: You lead teams of engineers and make sure projects get built safely and on time.
11-9041.day: Plan projects, pick and check designs, meet with clients and builders, and solve problems when something goes wrong.

17-2199.what: You are an engineer in a field that does not have its own special name.
17-2199.day: Analyse a problem, design a solution, test it, and work with other engineers to build it for real.

29-2072.what: You keep patients' medical records organised, accurate and safe.
29-2072.day: Enter and check medical information, answer questions from other staff, and protect patient privacy.

17-2141.what: You design machines, engines and structures that move and work safely.
17-2141.day: Turn an idea into a design, calculate how it will handle stress and heat, then test and improve it.

29-2057.what: You do eye-care jobs in a clinic, like taking eye measurements for glasses.
29-2057.day: Test patients' vision, prepare equipment and lenses, and support the eye doctor during procedures.

15-1251.what: You write the instructions that tell a computer what to do, step by step.
15-1251.day: Write and test code, fix errors, and update programs when something needs to change.

19-5011.what: You check workplaces for dangers and make sure people are safe and healthy.
19-5011.day: Visit workplaces, spot hazards, write reports, and suggest fixes before someone gets hurt.

51-4121.what: You join metal parts together using heat, to build frames, pipes, cars and ships.
51-4121.day: Set up your equipment, join pieces to plan, inspect your work, and follow safety rules.

17-2011.what: You design aircraft, rockets and the parts that make them fly safely.
17-2011.day: Work out how a design will handle stress and heat, build and test models, and check the maths behind every part.

15-1231.what: You fix computer network problems, like slow internet or dropped connections.
15-1231.day: Track down where a problem is happening, repair or replace equipment, and check the fix works.

29-2032.what: You use sound waves to take pictures of inside the body.
29-2032.day: Explain the scan to the patient, run the machine, check the images, and write the report.

29-1126.what: You help people who have trouble breathing, from asthma to serious lung disease.
29-1126.day: Test lung function, give treatments, teach patients how to use their inhalers, and work with doctors on care plans.

15-2031.what: You use maths to help organisations make better decisions.
15-2031.day: Ask what question needs answering, build a model, test it against real data, and explain the options.

51-4041.what: You use machines to cut and shape metal into exact parts for machines and products.
51-4041.day: Read the drawing, set up the machine, cut the part, check it against the plan, and fix what is out of tolerance.

19-2041.what: You study how pollution and climate change affect land, water and wildlife.
19-2041.day: Collect samples, run tests in the lab, analyse the data, and write reports that help people make decisions.
19-2041.school: Biology, chemistry, earth science and statistics

15-1243.what: You design the way information is stored so big systems stay fast and safe.
15-1243.day: Plan how data should be organised, test how systems handle it, and fix slow or fragile parts.

29-1215.what: You are a doctor who looks after whole families, from babies to grandparents.
29-1215.day: Run appointments, treat common illnesses, give check-ups, and refer people to specialists when needed.
29-1215.school: Biology, chemistry, physics, then medical school

29-1021.what: You look after people's teeth and gums and fix problems with them.
29-1021.day: Examine teeth, take x-rays, fill or remove teeth, and help patients keep their mouths healthy.

17-2071.what: You design electrical systems for buildings, machines and power grids.
17-2071.day: Plan circuits and systems, calculate loads and safety margins, and check the work before it is built.

29-1216.what: You are a doctor who treats adults with illnesses across the body.
29-1216.day: Examine patients, work out what is wrong, order tests, treat them, and follow up in clinic.
29-1216.school: Biology, chemistry, physics, then medical school

29-2056.what: You help vets look after animals, doing the hands-on clinical work.
29-2056.day: Prepare animals for treatment, assist with surgery, run lab tests, and help keep the animals comfortable.

29-1031.what: You help people eat well and stay healthy through food and advice.
29-1031.day: Talk to patients about their health and food, build eating plans, and run programmes for groups.

29-2055.what: You support surgeons in an operating room during surgery.
29-2055.day: Prepare the operating room, hand the surgeon the right instruments, and keep everything sterile.

49-2098.what: You install and service alarms, cameras and security systems in homes and buildings.
49-2098.day: Plan where equipment goes, run cables, connect and test it, and show customers how to use it.

19-4031.what: You do lab work with chemicals, supporting scientists and production teams.
19-4031.day: Prepare solutions, run experiments or quality checks, record results carefully, and tidy the lab.

49-2022.what: You install and repair the equipment that carries phone, TV and internet signals.
49-2022.day: Climb poles and towers, run and connect cables, test signals, and repair broken lines.

19-1021.what: You study the chemistry of living things, like how cells work and how drugs act.
19-1021.day: Run experiments, use lab equipment, analyse results, and write up findings with other scientists.

49-9052.what: You climb and repair the cables and poles that carry telephone and internet lines.
49-9052.day: Climb, find the fault, splice and test cable, and restore service before too many people lose it.

29-2053.what: You support mental health care teams, helping patients with day-to-day treatment.
29-2053.day: Prepare for sessions, keep records, support group sessions, and help with referrals.

51-8031.what: You run the equipment that turns dirty water into clean drinking water.
51-8031.day: Monitor the plant, test the water at every stage, adjust the process, and keep detailed records.

29-2031.what: You help doctors test and treat the heart and blood vessels.
29-2031.day: Set up and run heart tests, prepare patients, watch for problems during tests, and write up results.

49-9062.what: You repair the medical machines hospitals rely on, from pumps to scanners.
49-9062.day: Diagnose the fault, order or fit parts, test the repair, and check the machine meets safety rules.

17-1011.what: You design buildings that are safe, useful and good to look at.
17-1011.day: Sketch ideas, make drawings and models, work with clients and engineers, and check plans follow building rules.

17-3011.what: You turn an engineer's design into precise drawings that builders can follow.
17-3011.day: Read the design, produce drawings and models, check measurements, and revise when the design changes.

15-1254.what: You build the websites people use every day.
15-1254.day: Write the code for pages, make them work on phones and laptops, test the links, and fix what breaks.

17-3023.what: You build and test electrical and electronic systems, working under an engineer.
17-3023.day: Read the plans, assemble and wire equipment, run tests, record the results and help fix problems.

15-1255.what: You design how websites and apps look and how people move through them.
15-1255.day: Sketch screens, make clickable versions, test them with real people, and improve them.

19-4099.what: You do lab and field work supporting scientists in biology, chemistry and earth science.
19-4099.day: Set up equipment, run standard tests, collect and prepare samples, and record results carefully.

29-2081.what: You help people find and fit glasses and contact lenses.
29-2081.day: Take eye measurements, talk customers through choices, order lenses, and fit and adjust glasses.

29-1131.what: You treat sick and injured animals.
29-1131.day: Examine animals, diagnose problems, do surgery or give medicine, and check on recovering patients.

49-3011.what: You repair and maintain aircraft and the parts that keep them flying.
49-3011.day: Inspect engines and systems, diagnose faults, replace worn parts, and record every job done.

17-2072.what: You design electronic circuits, from phones to medical equipment.
17-2072.day: Work out how the circuit should behave, test it, and improve the design when it does not work.

15-1242.what: You look after the databases where an organisation stores its information.
15-1242.day: Keep data safe and backed up, speed up slow queries, and make sure the right people can get what they need.

29-9021.what: You keep digital medical records safe and organised, and make sure the data is right.
29-9021.day: Check records for errors, protect sensitive information, train staff on the system, and solve data problems.

15-1221.what: You research new computing methods, like how machines can learn or how to store huge amounts of data.
15-1221.day: Read what other researchers have done, design experiments, build prototypes, and publish what you find.

51-8021.what: You operate and maintain the boilers and heating systems that keep buildings warm.
51-8021.day: Check gauges and readings, control the equipment, spot problems early, and follow safety procedures.

29-1041.what: You examine eyes and vision and prescribe glasses or contact lenses.
29-1041.day: Test eyesight, check eye health, write prescriptions, and fit lenses for patients.

29-1011.what: You treat problems with people's backs and joints without surgery.
29-1011.day: Examine patients, adjust the spine and joints, give advice on exercise, and track progress.

49-9051.what: You build and repair the high-voltage lines that carry electricity across the country.
49-9051.day: Climb towers, replace damaged equipment, test lines before they are switched back on, and work as a team.

19-4021.what: You do lab work with living organisms, like plants, cells and bacteria.
19-4021.day: Care for cultures, run experiments, look at samples under microscopes, and keep careful records.

29-1223.what: You treat mental health conditions with therapy and, sometimes, medicine.
29-1223.day: Assess patients, plan treatment, see people regularly, and work with other mental health teams.
29-1223.school: Psychology, biology and then medical or clinical training

49-2094.what: You repair industrial electrical and electronic equipment in factories and workshops.
49-2094.day: Diagnose faults on site, replace or repair components, test the equipment, and report the work.

29-1221.what: You are a doctor who treats babies, children and teenagers.
29-1221.day: Run child health clinics, vaccinate, treat common illnesses, and check children's growth and development.
29-1221.school: Biology, chemistry, physics, then medical school

15-2011.what: You work out how much money to set aside for risks, like insurance companies and pensions.
15-2011.day: Build mathematical models, test them against real data, and explain the risk to people who make decisions.

29-2035.what: You operate MRI scanners that take detailed pictures inside the body.
29-2035.day: Prepare the patient, run the scan, check the images for quality, and work with the radiologist.
